text.t: Glucose is a simple sugar with the formula C6H12O6: six carbons, twelve hydrogens and six oxygens.
Five carbons and one oxygen close into a six-sided ring.
In water, simple sugars like glucose are mostly found in ring form.
The sixth carbon sticks out of the ring and carries its own OH group.
Five OH groups stick out around the molecule.

does.t: Glucose is an important source of energy for humans.
During cellular respiration, cells release the energy in glucose and use it to make ATP.

shape.t: Glucose, galactose and fructose share the same formula, C6H12O6, but their atoms are arranged differently, so they differ chemically.
This model is alpha-D-glucopyranose, one of glucose's ring forms.

text.t: Plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
Animals that eat plants often get glucose by breaking down starch.
Insulin tells liver, muscle and fat cells to take glucose out of the blood.

wrong.t: When insulin does not work properly, glucose builds up in the blood, a condition called diabetes mellitus.

compare.t: From its farthest atom to its farthest atom, glucose measures about 0.8 nm.
A water molecule, the smallest in this gallery, measures about 0.16 nm.
